reading.body:
EY's own material describes a gap between how fast organizations deploy AI and how slowly their controls catch up.

The pattern is a services firm selling governance and risk work alongside the AI deployment it advises on. EY says it consolidated its generative AI work into a global agentic AI platform, and it promotes survey material on agentic AI risk, cybersecurity, shadow AI, and measuring return on investment beyond token costs. The two halves reinforce each other: the more autonomous systems a client runs, the more assurance, tax, and transformation work follows.

For AI specifically, this is a demand signal rather than a supply one. The constraint EY names is organizational, not physical. Its cited survey of senior AI executives found processes and controls lagging deployment, which is a statement about how firms absorb AI, not about whether they can power it. Nothing here speaks to compute, data centers, or electricity.

What the data does not cover is scale. There are no client counts, revenue figures, headcount, or dates attached to the platform or the surveys. The profile is a description of services and marketing positions, verified on 2026-10-01, and it should be read as what EY says about itself rather than as measured outcomes.

profile_text.body:
EY provides consulting, assurance, tax and transaction services, which the company says help solve clients' toughest challenges and build a better working world for all. Its US site organizes that work under service areas including Artificial Intelligence, Strategy, Transaction & Transformation, Audit, Tax Function Operations, and Climate Change & Sustainability.

On AI, the company says it unified its GenAI breakthroughs into a global agentic AI platform that changes how people work and how clients accelerate AI at scale. Its site promotes an EY AI Risk and Governance Survey covering AI governance, agentic AI risk, cybersecurity and what it calls a confidence gap, along with material on measuring agentic AI return on investment beyond token costs. A survey of senior AI executives cited by EY found that organizations are rapidly deploying AI and autonomous systems while their processes and controls are not keeping pace, despite reputational, cybersecurity and shadow AI risk. Marna Ricker, EY Global Vice Chair - Tax, is quoted on tax leaders moving beyond policy to shape strategy amid supply chain shifts and AI-driven change.

The company is listed as a for-profit business operating from ey.com/en_us.
